name: Topilutamide (Fluridil)

lead: Topilutamide (fluridil) is a scalp-applied antiandrogen sold as Eucapil in the Czech Republic and Slovakia for pattern hair loss in men and women. People interested in topical alternatives to oral DHT blockers discuss it.

It blocks the androgen receptor in the scalp, so follicles are less affected by DHT and thin more slowly. It is reported to break down quickly in human serum. Published data consists of small older studies and lab work; no large randomized trials were found.

paras: It is used as a 2% lotion applied to the scalp, regularly over months. Users often pair it with other hair-loss measures.
Safety data are limited. It is not approved by the FDA or EMA for hair loss.

angle.text: Topilutamide blocks androgen receptors at the scalp, so follicles shrink less under DHT and thinning slows. Users interested in topical options instead of oral DHT blockers discuss it. It is sold in two European countries, and published trial data is small.

lead: Topilutamide, also called fluridil (code BP-766), is a topical nonsteroidal antiandrogen applied to the scalp for pattern hair loss in men and women. It is marketed as a 2% product, Eucapil, by Interpharma Praha [1][2].
Wikipedia describes it as approved for cosmetic use in Europe and sold only in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, with no FDA or EMA approval for androgenetic alopecia [1].
Evidence is limited to preclinical receptor studies and older small clinical reports described in secondary sources; the sources reviewed give no quantitative trial results [1].

paras: Topilutamide is used on the scalp for androgenetic alopecia [1]. Wikipedia notes that finasteride and minoxidil are the only drugs approved for the condition in major jurisdictions, and that topilutamide lacks FDA and EMA approval for it [1].

It is an androgen receptor antagonist of the perfluoroacylamido-arylpropanamide class, structurally related to flutamide and bicalutamide [1]. Wikipedia reports that it has higher receptor affinity than bicalutamide and hydroxyflutamide and suppressed androgen receptor by about 96% in prostate cancer cells at 10 micromolar, but notes that these findings need validation. It degrades in human serum with a half-life of about 6 hours, and breakdown products were undetectable in human serum in studies, which is the basis for claims of low systemic exposure [1].

Wikipedia mentions a 9-month open study in women and a clinical study in men, both described as showing benefit and safety, but gives no quantitative results and relies on older sources [1]. No randomized controlled trial was found in the sources reviewed.
Topilutamide was introduced for medical use in 2003 and its patent expired in 2020 [1].

timeline.event: Introduced for medical (cosmetic) use in Europe [1].
